⭐️ SEC eyes enforcement action over prediction market insider trading 

🔖 The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has warned that prediction markets offering contracts linked to corporate earnings and business performance could face enforcement action over insider trading, fraud and market manipulation. SEC Enforcement Director David Woodcock said the agency was monitoring activity on prediction platforms and expected to pursue potential securities violations. He added that enforcement activity was likely “in the future, for sure,” although he did not identify a particular company or announce new charges.

➡️ Woodcock’s comments centered on contracts that allow traders to bet on financial results or key performance indicators, commonly known as KPIs. Such products can involve outcomes tied to quarterly earnings, sales figures or other measures of a listed company’s business performance. The SEC oversees securities markets, while the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) regulates many derivatives contracts. Prediction markets can raise questions about which agency has authority when a contract’s outcome depends on a publicly traded company.

🔔 The regulator has already approved a Cboe Global Markets proposal involving binary options tied to corporate performance measures. The contracts allow traders to take positions on outcomes such as Citigroup’s earnings per share or Apple’s iPhone sales revenue. The decision addressed Cboe’s particular products and did not establish that every prediction contract involving a company’s performance automatically falls under SEC jurisdiction.

A vulnerability in the Remote Access SSL VPN service of Cisco Secure Firewall Adaptive Security Appliance (ASA) Software and Cisco Secure Firewall Threat Defense (FTD) Software could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to cause the device to reload unexpectedly, resulting in a denial of service (DoS) condition.
This vulnerability is due to logic errors when secondary authentication is configured on a tunnel group. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a crafted request when connecting to the SSL remote access VPN. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to cause the affected device to reload, resulting in a DoS condition. 

Cisco has released software updates that address this vulnerability. There are no workarounds that address this vulnerability.
This advisory is available at the following link:

🚀 Want to Become a Generative AI Engineer in 2026? Here’s Your Learning Roadmap.

GenAI is evolving fast. You don’t need 50 courses or every framework. Master these 10 skills in sequence. 👇

1️⃣ Transformers & LLM Fundamentals
Learn transformer architecture, self-attention, Q/K/V, multi-head attention, masking, tokenization, context windows, positional encoding, and how LLMs generate responses.
📚 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZhAz268Hdpw&t=784s

Understand embeddings, semantic similarity, cosine similarity, nearest-neighbor search, vector indexing, and databases such as FAISS, Chroma, and Pinecone.

3️⃣ Prompt Engineering & Structured Outputs
Learn zero-shot and few-shot prompting, system prompts, context engineering, JSON outputs, prompt optimization, tool calling, and validation.

4️⃣ Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)
Master document ingestion, chunking, embeddings, semantic and hybrid retrieval, metadata filtering, reranking, grounded responses, citations, and evaluation.
📚 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4Ax77tnW0e8
📚 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=X0btK9X0Xnk

Connect models with data, tools, and application logic using integrations, prompt templates, retrievers, structured outputs, RAG pipelines, and workflows.

6️⃣ LangGraph & Agentic AI
Build stateful workflows using nodes, edges, state management, conditional routing, memory, human approval, tool execution, error recovery, and multi-agent orchestration.
📚 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yC36gN-rqjo&list=PLKnIA16_RmvYsvB8qkUQuJmJNuiCUJFPL

7️⃣ Cloud AI & Production Deployment
Explore Microsoft Foundry, Amazon Bedrock, model hosting, inference APIs, enterprise RAG, agent deployment, observability, monitoring, scaling, cost optimization, and access control.

Learn RAGAS, LLM-as-a-Judge, faithfulness, answer relevance, hallucination detection, prompt injection, data leakage, PII protection, testing, and regression evaluation.

📌 Kerman, IRNA – The spokesperson for the Islamic Revolution Guards Corps (IRGC), referring to a recent order from the Leader of the Islamic Revolution to respond swiftly and forcefully to any new aggression, says the removal of geographical limits in targeting enemies paves the way for complete deterrence.

Addressing a ceremony of an IRGC security unit in Kerman Province on Sunday, Brigadier General Hossein Mohebbi welcomed the order from Commander-in-Chief Ayatollah Sayyid Mojtaba Hosseini Khamenei to senior military commanders on countering aggressors.
​
Stating that the Leader's directives have “opened a new chapter in the war,” he said the Iranian Armed Forces are now more prepared than before to deliver a decisive response to the enemy.
​
Mohebbi added that the IRGC has already placed the identification of new targets and the planning of operations across new geographical areas on its agenda.
​
Iran is engaged in a battle with one of the world's most militarily powerful nations which, he noted, in collusion with the vilest terrorist entity—the Zionist regime—waged wars against the Iranian nation.
​
What matters most, however, he continued, is Iran's victory over the aggressors, a reference to the two wars imposed by the US and the Israeli regime over the past two years. “Our victory lay in preventing the enemy from attaining its objectives,” he added.
​
Referring to the US pretexts for its presence in the region, he said Washington's justification of providing security proved futile as it failed to keep the Strait of Hormuz open—even for a few days or a few hours—despite possessing the world's largest navy.
​

Crypto Idea

While the rest of the world is talking about the Binance hack, something is happening in the U.S. stock market that could turn out to be far more important for investors.

Alphabet lost around 13% in a single trading session, wiping out nearly $500 billion in market value and leaving the stock roughly 30% below its 52-week high. Yet, at first glance, the earnings report itself looked very strong. Google Cloud more than doubled its revenue, demand for AI continues to grow, and Cloud's future contracted revenue has already surpassed $560 billion.

But the market looked beyond the headline numbers. Google's core advertising business grew more slowly than expected, and, more importantly, the company has now reported negative free cash flow for the second consecutive quarter. In the most recent quarter alone, the company spent roughly $9 billion more than it actually generated after all expenses. The reason is the same as before: massive investments in AI, data centers, and its own chips.

And this is where an important shift has taken place. For the past few years, seeing rapid growth in AI-related business was enough for the market to forgive almost any level of spending. Now investors are starting to ask a different question. Not how quickly AI is growing, but how much actual cash a company has left after that growth.

And the problem goes far beyond Google. Alphabet currently accounts for around 5% of the entire S&P 500 and more than 8% of the Nasdaq 100. The seven largest tech companies together make up roughly 35% of the S&P 500. Yesterday, around 80% of the companies in the index were up, yet the S&P 500 still ended the day lower, largely because of Alphabet's decline.

So the biggest risk right now isn't that Google has turned into a bad company. On the contrary, its business remains massive and continues to grow rapidly. The real risk is market concentration. If investors start reassessing AI spending across the other tech giants in the same way, a correction in just a handful of companies could drag down the entire index. And even someone who simply bought the S&P 500 for diversification could suddenly realize just how much of their money actually depends on a few technology companies.

It raises more questions than it answers: first, the shark wasn’t actually caught—it was dragged ashore, a rarity in itself. And second, the creature was badly wounded, yet the wound looked more than a month old.
